market_read: Week 13 snapshot: 11 verified rows (0 new, 11 persisting, 0 gone), 0 indicative. The market freeze extends to 13 consecutive weeks with no price movements, no new unique listings, and no confirmed clearances across any monitored municipality. Pagsanjan-core holds 4 rows (Lambac PHP 850/sqm, Pinagsanjan PHP 1,100/sqm, Sabang PHP 1,500/sqm, Maulawin PHP 2,000/sqm); Pagsanjan-core median PHP 1,300/sqm. Ring municipalities continue to cluster at PHP 2,000/sqm or above, except Pila Mojon at PHP 269/sqm which likely reflects distressed or off-market conditions. A new development this week: the Cavinti Caliraya 8,394 sqm lot is now listed by at least three separate agents — one at PHP 18,500,000 (tracked) and one at PHP 23,503,200 (tracked) — with a Lumban listing explicitly citing a prior price of PHP 23.5M before reduction, suggesting the higher-priced listing may eventually drop. This multi-agent fragmentation points to a motivated seller who has not yet attracted a buyer. The 13-week absence of new entrants, price reductions (except the probable Cavinti lot), and confirmed clearances points to sellers anchored to aspirational prices with no buyer pressure. For a raw 0.5–1 ha Pagsanjan parcel, recommended asking range PHP 1,400–1,800/sqm; fastest-sale price PHP 900–1,000/sqm. Aging-versus-cleared inventory remains unanswerable without confirmed sales data.
